BiblicalUsage: To hasten is to press forward in a hurry, and the priests thrust Uzziah out of the temple when leprosy breaks out on his forehead. The posts hurry out with Haman's decree, and Mordecai hurries home in sorrow, and the posts hasten again with the counter-decree that saves the Jews. The word is speed under pressure, and it carries both judgment and deliverance.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe haste in Esther is the picture of a world out of control, and God's hand moving faster still. The decree of death goes out in haste, and the decree of life goes out in haste, and the second one wins. I hold that God is never late, even when the posts are running.
